summary.text: A 36-year-old woman with SLE, off medication for years, presented with several days of fever, malaise, cough, arthralgia and myalgia; she was febrile and tachycardic with WBC 21 K/UL and right lower lobe consolidation, and was started on antibiotics with initial improvement.

On hospital day 3 she developed acute confusion, hallucinations and worsening mental status requiring intubation; CT head, MRI brain and EEG were unremarkable or negative, and she was later extubated with persistent impaired mental status.
Autoantibody and complement labs and CSF studies were obtained; infectious causes were ruled out and lupus psychosis due to NPSLE was suspected.

She received pulse-dose steroids and cyclophosphamide per the NIH protocol with significant mental status improvement, completed six months of cyclophosphamide with a steroid taper, started hydroxychloroquine, and has remained clinically stable off steroids.

summary.text: A 32-year-old woman with no prior medical history presented with one week of worsening abdominal pain, nausea and vomiting, after an earlier outside-hospital visit and a told diagnosis of abdominal lymphadenopathy, with a chronic malar rash and progressive vision loss.

Examination showed malar plaques, periorbital edema and reduced vision; imaging showed extensive mesenteric and retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy, labs pancytopenia and positive autoantibodies, ophthalmology retinal vasculitis, and brain MRI multiple infarcts, with elevated CSF protein, negative infectious workup and no vascular occlusion on MRA.

Lupus-induced cerebral vasculitis was suspected; she was treated with pulse-dose steroids and cyclophosphamide per NIH protocol with good clinical response and is in remission on azathioprine after completing cyclophosphamide and a steroid taper.

summary.text: A 38-year-old woman with a history of pituitary adenoma, leiomyoma with partial hysterectomy and pelvic inflammatory disease presented with two days of hallucinations; she had recently established rheumatologic care for positive ANA, facial rash and photosensitivity, with positive anti-Smith and anti-RNP antibodies and low complement.

On admission she was mute and unable to provide history and psychiatry diagnosed catatonia; brain imaging was unremarkable, labs showed persistent anemia and leukopenia, CSF showed mildly elevated protein, and infectious causes were ruled out.

She was started on hydroxychloroquine, mycophenolate mofetil and reduced pulse-dose methylprednisolone; IV benzodiazepines gave no improvement, ECT produced dramatic improvement, and she is managed on mycophenolate 1,000 mg BID with hydroxychloroquine discontinued for congenital retinal abnormalities, with stable mental status and no recurrence.
